set.body:
Phase 1 of docs/plan.md. The owner's rule, 19 November 2026: the technical core is in place and rock solid before any user journey begins. When the journeys begin, we believe they will pass.

This item closes when every line below is true at one commit on main. Rock solid means this list and nothing else. A new check needs the owner's yes.

1. Built. Every engine, tool and deployment capability the journeys need is done: IN2, IN3, IN4, IN5 (intake); SEE2, SEE3, SEE5, SEE7 (catalog, search, tables, the multi-modal fixture); SHARE2 (download); OPEN1, OPEN2, OPEN3, OPEN4 (readiness, publishing tools, Neurobagel); RUN2, RUN3 (deployment, backup and restore).
2. Journey scripts. CORE1 is green on hosted CI for five consecutive runs on main.
3. Real data. CORE2: every dataset in the pinned corpus imports cleanly or fails with a finding that names the file and the fix.
4. Scale. CORE3 and CORE4: the frozen workload and a pilot-sized study meet the stated budgets, and the service refuses clearly beyond its stated limits.
5. Access. CORE5: every read route is tested against every level of access.
6. Known defects. CORE6, CORE7 and CORE8 are closed.
7. The whole gate is green on hosted CI at that commit: sbt check, the PostgreSQL suites, the console checks and the packaged-service checks.

What this gate blocks
The rehearsals with people (SEE8, SHARE5, OPEN5), the pre-flight on the pilot host (RUN5) and, through it, the first real study (IN6).

What it does not block
The console screens (SEE1, SEE4, SEE6, SHARE1, SHARE3, IN7, OPEN6). They are designed and built alongside, on engine pieces that are already done. The owner's tasks also continue.
set.title: CORE: The technical core is in place and proven before any journey begins
